guides.title: The Career Change Play: Map Your Transferable Proof, Close the Real Gaps, and Explain the Switch in One Sentence
guides.blurb: A step-by-step play to find what already transfers from your background, name the gaps that actually matter, and say why you're switching in one clear sentence.
inside: How to pick a target role specific enough to plan around
A prompt that turns your past work into proof the new field recognizes
A way to sort real gaps from imagined ones
A one-sentence switch story you can use everywhere
How to run the full skill-gap plan with Claude and Scout
A short action plan to close each gap, starting this week
guides.intro:
If you want to switch careers, you've probably looked at a job posting and thought, my experience doesn't line up. Usually it lines up more than you think. The trouble is that most career changers undersell the work they've already done, and when someone asks why they're switching, the answer comes out long and apologetic.

This play fixes both. You'll sort your background into proof that transfers and gaps that are real. You'll pick the fastest honest way to close each gap. Then you'll write a switch story you can say in one sentence. The first three steps work with any AI chat. The later steps show you how to do it faster with Claude and Scout. No play guarantees a switch. This one helps you make your strongest, clearest case.

free.body:
Before anything else, get specific. A field like tech or healthcare is too wide to plan around. Pick one role title you'd actually apply for, like customer success manager or UX researcher.

Now find 3 to 5 real job postings for that role. Copy the full text of each one. You're looking for what shows up again and again, because repeated requirements are the ones that matter most.

Paste the postings into ChatGPT or Claude with the prompt below. Keep the output. You'll use it in every step that follows.
free.prompt:
I'm planning a career change into [target role]. Below are [number] real job postings for this role. Read all of them and give me:

1. The skills and experience that appear in most of the postings
2. Any licenses, certifications, or degrees that are listed as required (not just preferred)
3. The tools or software that come up more than once
4. The words and phrases these employers use to describe strong candidates

Only list what is actually in the postings. Don't add anything.

Postings:
[paste job postings here]
free.title: Step 1: Pick one target role and pull its real requirements

free.body:
Next, take inventory. List what you've actually done in your current or past roles. Be concrete. Write things like ran weekly reporting for a team of 12, or handled the hardest customer escalations. Skip job titles and focus on the work.

Then ask AI to match your work to the requirements from Step 1, using the new field's language. This is where most career changers find proof they didn't know they had.

Read the output carefully. Cut anything that stretches the truth. Proof only works if you can back it up in an interview.
free.prompt:
I'm moving from [current field or role] into [target role]. Here are the requirements I pulled from real job postings:
[paste your Step 1 output]

Here is what I've actually done in my work:
[list your concrete tasks, projects, and results]

For each requirement, tell me:
1. Which of my experiences is real proof for it, rewritten in the language this field uses
2. How strong that proof is: strong, partial, or none

Don't invent experience I didn't list. If I have no proof for something, say so plainly.
free.title: Step 2: Turn your past work into proof

free.body:
When someone asks why you're changing careers, you need an answer you can say in one breath. A good switch story connects where you've been to where you're going. It doesn't apologize for the move.

The simple shape is: I've been doing [what you did], and the part I'm best at is [the transferable strength], which is why I'm moving into [new role].

Use the prompt below to get a few versions. Say each one out loud. Keep the one that sounds like you.
free.prompt:
Help me write a one-sentence answer to the question, why are you switching careers?

I'm moving from [current field or role] into [target role].
My strongest transferable proof is: [paste the strongest items from Step 2]
The real reason I want this change: [your honest reason]

Write 5 versions. Each one must be a single sentence, sound natural when spoken, connect my past work to the new role, and not apologize for or downplay my background. Don't overstate my experience.
free.title: Step 3: Draft your switch story in one sentence

locked.body:
Steps 1 to 3 work, but they take time. Scout does the same play in one pass inside Claude. It gives you a skill-gap plan: your transferable proof, the real gaps, the fastest way to close each one, and your switch story.

First, add Scout to Claude on your computer using this link: https://scoutjob.ai/start?app=claude&ref=jobsearchplaybook-hub&utm_source=jobsearchplaybook&utm_medium=creator-hub&utm_campaign=plan-a-career-change&utm_content=angelica

Then open a new chat in Claude and paste the prompt below. Fill in the field you're moving into. A quick heads-up: Scout is free for 7 days with a card, then $97/month. So pick your one target role from Step 1 before you run it.
locked.prompt: Scout, I want to move into [new field]. What from my background transfers, what's missing, and how do I explain the switch?
locked.title: Step 4: Run the full skill-gap plan with Claude and Scout

locked.body:
Look at the gaps from your Scout plan, or from your Step 2 output if you're doing this by hand. Sort each gap into one of two buckets.

Bucket one is required credentials. If the field requires a license, certification, or degree, plan to get it. Don't look for a way around it. Bucket two is skills you can show. These can often be closed with a short course, a small project, volunteer work, or taking on a task in your current job.

For each gap, pick one action you can start this week. Use the prompt below to turn your gaps into a simple plan.
locked.prompt:
I'm moving into [target role]. Here are my gaps:
[paste the gaps from Scout or from Step 2]

For each gap:
1. Tell me if it's a required credential for this field or a skill I can show another way
2. If it's a required credential, tell me what it is and the usual way people earn it. Don't suggest skipping it.
3. If it's a skill, suggest the fastest realistic way to build and show it, like a small project, a course, or volunteer work
4. Give me one first action I can take this week

Put it in a simple list ordered from the quickest gap to close to the longest. Don't make up timelines or costs. If you're not sure, say so.
locked.title: Step 5: Sort your gaps and pick the fastest honest fix

locked.body:
Your one-sentence story only helps if people see it. Use it in four places: your LinkedIn headline and About section, the top of your resume, your cover letters, and your answer to tell me about yourself.

Each place needs a slightly different length, but the core message should stay the same. That consistency is what makes the switch make sense to a hiring manager.

Use the prompt below to adapt your story for each spot.
locked.prompt:
Here is my one-sentence switch story:
[paste your story from Step 3 or from Scout]

Here is my strongest transferable proof:
[paste 3 to 5 proof points]

I'm targeting [target role]. Using the same core message, write:
1. A LinkedIn headline under 220 characters
2. A LinkedIn About section of 3 short paragraphs
3. A 2 to 3 line resume summary
4. A 30-second spoken answer to, tell me about yourself

Keep it plain and specific. Don't overstate my experience or add skills I didn't list.
locked.title: Step 6: Put your switch story to work everywhere

locked.body:
Before you send out applications, say your switch story to 2 or 3 people who already work in your target role. Former coworkers, alumni, or LinkedIn connections all work. Keep the ask small: 15 minutes and one question.

Ask them: does my background make sense for this role, and what would make it stronger? Write down what they say. If two people point out the same gap, move it to the top of your plan from Step 5.

Use the prompt below to write a short, respectful message asking for the conversation.
locked.prompt:
Write a short LinkedIn message to [name], who works as a [their role] at [company]. I'm moving from [current field] into [target role].

I'd like 15 minutes of their time to get honest feedback on whether my background fits the role. Mention one specific thing about them: [something you know about their work or path].

Keep it under 80 words. Be polite and direct. Don't ask for a job or a referral.
locked.title: Step 7: Test your story with people already in the field

guides.tip: Before you share your switch story, read it next to the requirements list from Step 1. Every claim in your story should point to a requirement in those postings. If a line doesn't connect to anything the employer asked for, cut it and put your strongest proof point in its place.

guides.title: Find your next career path with Claude + Scout
guides.blurb: Play: Pick a direction before you send another application. When you finish, you'll have 2 to 3 adjacent roles to look at, the evidence for each from your own experience, and the gap you'd need to close for each.
inside: Start a new chat and set the scene
Have Scout do it for you
guides.intro: Most people who feel lost apply to everything. Nothing feels like a clear fit, so every posting looks possible. The trouble is that a scattered search can read as unfocused to the person reading your application. A short list of roles, each backed by evidence, gives you something to aim at.

free.title: Step 1: Gather your raw material (5 minutes)
free.body:
You can run this play with any AI chat, ChatGPT or Claude. No Scout needed.

Open a document. Paste in your resume, or write down your last 2 to 3 roles. Add the tasks you did most, the tools you used, and the work people came to you for.

free.title: Step 2: Start a new chat and set the scene
free.body: Paste this, then add your material below it:
free.prompt:
I'm trying to figure out which roles I should be going for. I'll paste my work history below. Don't suggest anything yet. First, read it and list the 5 skills or strengths that show up most often, with one example from my history for each. Then wait for my reply.

[Paste your resume or work history here]

free.title: Step 3: Check the list
free.body: Read what comes back. Fix anything wrong. Add anything missing. This list is your evidence base, so make it accurate.

free.title: Step 4: Ask for adjacent roles
free.prompt:
Based on the strengths we just listed, which roles fit my experience that I haven't considered? Give me 2 to 3 roles that sit close to what I've already done. For each one, tell me:
1. Why it fits, using specific examples from my history.
2. The gap: what I'd still need to show or learn to be a credible candidate.
Do not include salary figures. If a role is a stretch, say so.

locked.title: Step 5: Pressure-test each role
locked.prompt: For the role [ROLE NAME], what would a recruiter look for on a resume that I don't have yet? What is one small thing I could do in the next 30 days to start closing that gap?

locked.title: Step 6: Pick one to test
locked.body: Choose the role that feels most workable, not the one that sounds best. Search for 5 job postings for it. Check how many of the requirements you already meet. If it feels right, aim your resume and applications at that one role for the next few weeks.

locked.title: Step 7: Have Scout do it for you
locked.body:
Scout works from your CareerID, so it already has your experience in hand. You skip the gathering and the back-and-forth.

1. Add Scout to Claude on your computer with this link: https://scoutjob.ai/start?app=claude&ref=jobsearchplaybook-hub&utm_source=jobsearchplaybook&utm_medium=creator-hub&utm_campaign=find-your-next-career-path&utm_content=angelica

2. Open a new chat and paste this prompt:

3. What you'll see: Scout's path check. It gives you 2 to 3 adjacent roles, the evidence for each from your CareerID, and the gap for each.

What it costs: Scout is free for 7 days with a card, then $97/month. If you want to try the play first, the do-it-yourself steps above cost nothing.
locked.prompt: Scout, which roles fit my experience that I haven't considered?

guides.tip: Treat the gap as your next move, not a verdict. When you get your roles back, look at the gap line first. Ask: "Can I close this in 30 days, or does it need a longer plan?" Then pick the role with the gap you can start closing this week. Write that one gap at the top of your notes and work on it before you apply anywhere. A search with one clear target is easier to run and easier for a recruiter to follow.
